AI materials discoveries: predictions and experiments

233 discoveries from 2020 to 2026

From prediction to physical evidence

  • GNoME used a graph neural network to predict crystal structures and estimate stability. The project reports that other laboratories synthesized some of the predicted structures.
  • A-Lab used an automated laboratory to make compounds from computed targets. The catalog record links the correction and explains where the diffraction evidence remained inconclusive.
  • The HoB₂ magnetocaloric study used machine learning to select a known compound. The study reports measurements of its magnetic entropy change under an applied field.

These studies illustrate distinct steps. A calculation estimates stability, synthesis produces a sample, and a property measurement tests a defined characteristic under stated conditions. For claims about performance, check which property was measured and what it was compared with.

About AI discoveries in materials

This selection contains 233 catalog entries dated 4 Feb 2020 to 18 Nov 2026. 233 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

18 Nov 2026Seoul National University; Korea Institute for Advanced Study

XCAPE proposes nine previously unmatched crystal structure assignments

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In an arXiv preprint, researchers used XCAPE and the SevenNet-Omni machine learning interatomic potential to revisit existing powder X-ray diffraction patterns. In the subset without matching reference structures, they reported nine plausible atomic arrangements, eight halides and one sulfide, that met diffraction and energy criteria. These are inferred structural assignments from existing measurements and computed energies. The preprint does not establish that the assignments are unique or independently confirmed.

Technology: SevenNet-Omni machine learning interatomic potential (XCAPE)

Editorial relevance 47 materials Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
SevenNet-Omni evaluated energies and relaxed candidate structures during the evolutionary search, supporting selection of candidates for comparison with measured diffraction.
Test and result
Existing powder diffraction patterns were compared with predictions, using an energy criterion to assess plausibility. The nine assignments are the subset reported in Section 2.5.
Limitation / still unknown
Unique assignment and independent experimental confirmation were not established in the reviewed preprint.

13 Nov 2026Tsinghua University; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Binzhou Institute of Technology

Machine-learned potentials resolve a disorder trade-off in lithium cathode transport

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using actively fine-tuned machine-learning interatomic potentials with experimental validation, the authors report that cation disorder improves lithium-path connectivity but broadens site energies, suppressing diffusion in disordered-rocksalt cathodes. They develop an energy-adjusted percolation descriptor and a Li–Mn–Ti–O design map. This is a composition-specific transport result; the review does not assign individual capacity figures to modeled or measured material states.

29 Oct 2026Washington State University; Australian Synchrotron, ANSTO; Prince Sattam bin Abdulaziz University

X-ray analysis found a molecular tilt gradient at a buried transistor interface

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An optical model built with hierarchical clustering helped researchers infer a distinct molecular state at the buried interface of a zinc phthalocyanine film on silica. Fitting resonant soft X-ray reflectivity gave a molecular tilt of about 38° at the interface and 69.6° in the bulk, with an interface transition length of about 1.49 nanometers. The inference depends on the optical and structural models. A second film supported the density gradient, while its measurement could not independently resolve orientation. The results are from the October 29 revision of an October 22 arXiv preprint.

Technology: Hierarchical agglomerative clustering; ML-DFT optical model

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Hierarchical clustering converted calculated electronic transition dipoles into a compact optical representation, refined against independent absorption measurements, for the depth-dependent reflectivity model.
Test and result
The researchers collected energy- and polarization-dependent soft X-ray reflectivity, compared discrete-layer and gradient fits and assessed sensitivity. Diffraction informed the structural interpretation; independent-film nonresonant reflectivity checked density.
Limitation / still unknown
The angle and gradient depend on the fitted model. The second film did not independently establish orientation, and alternative microscopic packing mechanisms were not fully resolved.

22 Oct 2026Kyonggi University; Seoul National University; Dongguk University; Korea University

Surface-informed active learning selects a tested Ni55Co10Fe35 oxygen-evolution catalyst

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Researchers used Gaussian-process active learning with DFT adsorption energies to select a nickel–cobalt–iron alloy precursor. Synthesized Ni55Co10Fe35 required 327 mV overpotential at 10 mA/cm² in alkaline laboratory tests, versus 380 mV for NiFe and 404 mV for CoFe controls. Its Tafel slope was 43.07 mV/decade. Prediction and experimental activity maps did not fully agree; this supports compositional narrowing, not quantitative performance prediction. The working surface reconstructs into oxyhydroxides, which the alloy-surface model does not represent.

Technology: Gaussian-process regression; surface-informed active learning

22 Oct 2026University of Houston; Purdue University

Learned structural screening enables a comparative sodium-cathode redox map

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Machine-learned interatomic energies screened stacking candidates before first-principles calculations across fifteen sodium layered-oxide chemistries. The resulting comparative map found a largely partner-independent order of redox couples, explaining modeled charge transfer and oxidation sequences. These are conditional computational relationships, not newly measured battery performance.

Technology: MACE-OMAT-0 medium machine-learning interatomic potential

Editorial relevance 40 materials Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
MACE relaxes and ranks stacking alternatives, determining which candidates proceed to first-principles analysis; downstream redox interpretation uses those selected structures.
Test and result
More than 120,000 candidate structures screened before 1,025 first-principles calculations; five single-metal and ten equimolar mixed-metal chemistries. Selected comparisons use previously published measurements.
Limitation / still unknown
Restricted ordering library, selected stackings and equimolar mixtures; zero-temperature energetics omit entropy and kinetic effects. Learned preselection may miss alternatives. Moment-derived oxidation states have covalency ambiguity and some experimental disagreements. No cycling-performance or universal composition prediction is established.

20 Oct 2026Eindhoven University of Technology

AI-guided simulations rank two zeolites differently as CO₂ pressure changes

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: RaspAssistant compared three literature-based adsorption models against existing MFI zeolite measurements, selected the one with the lowest aggregate error and used it to simulate CO₂ adsorption in 197 pure-silica structures. JBW had the highest simulated uptake at 1 kPa, while GIS led at 10 and 100 kPa and had the highest calculated working capacity from 1 to 100 kPa. These are model-dependent rankings of known structures. The reference measurements were for MFI.

Technology: RaspAssistant; GPT-5.2; GPT-5.4

Family GPT-5: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 40 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The GPT-5.2 supervisor and GPT-based specialists compared candidate force fields with reference measurements, selected the model for the larger screen, coordinated simulations and analyzed pressure-specific rankings.
Test and result
Three force-field combinations were compared against existing MFI adsorption isotherms at three temperatures. The selected model was used for 2,955 adsorption calculations on 197 structures. The outcome is relative simulated uptake and working capacity in the specified screening study.
Limitation / still unknown
Quantitative transfer from MFI to other frameworks was not established. The screened candidates were not retested experimentally in this case study, and reported descriptors could not identify a pore-scale mechanism. Prior work already considered GIS and JBW for carbon capture.

The GLONet maps random latent vectors to multilayer designs, optimizing per-layer refractive/material parameters and thickness using differentiable optical simulations to maximize broadband absorption. The demonstrated result is a fabricated device under p-polarized illumination at a 49° incidence angle using a prism-coupled ENZ mode; it is not an angle-independent or application-qualified absorber. Earlier work by the same group used neural networks to design homogeneous ITO stacks; this paper reports a distinct heterogeneous ITO/AZO design with experimental validation. No commercial application is demonstrated.

Learned constitutive fitting identifies a composition–age tradeoff in hydrogel mechanics

Technology: Gaussian-process surrogate Bayesian optimization with expected improvement for constitutive coefficient fitting

Editorial relevance 33 materials Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned Gaussian-process surrogate adaptively searched constitutive parameters against measured curves, enabling coefficient-level composition analysis and the represented mechanical tradeoff beyond reporting optimizer convergence alone.
Test and result
Experimental rheology curves from basal-membrane and fibrin/matrix hydrogel formulations were fitted with a second-order polynomial hyperelastic model. A Gaussian-process surrogate learned fit error across coefficient settings and expected improvement selected subsequent finite-element evaluations. Statistical analysis of fitted coefficients supported a concentration/source-age compensation at low to moderate strain; the higher-strain coefficient effects were not statistically established.
Limitation / still unknown
Fit error is agreement to the same experimental curves, not held-out prediction. Constitutive assumptions, coefficient dependence and small replicate sets constrain mechanistic interpretation. Variability intervals were adjusted for physical plausibility rather than uniformly calibrated predictive coverage. Some compositional trends recover prior literature; the admitted result is the specific combined tradeoff, not first discovery that concentration or age affects stiffness. New formulations, cell behavior, tissue function and in-vivo benefit were not independently tested.

The original abstract specifically attributes earliest discovery of all three newly reported ternary-only phases to aLLoyM-guided initial measurements; a general-purpose LLM chose a textbook-like measurement strategy that efficiently found a larger number of phases in fewer cycles.
Test and result
Researchers used an LLM to plan iterative composition measurements and experimentally mapped the Co–Al–Ge phase diagram at 900 °C.
Limitation / still unknown
This source is an arXiv preprint, not a peer-reviewed journal publication as of the checked record. The source abstract supports the reported ternary phase-diagram result and three phases described as novel and ternary-only, but does not provide their formulas or independent replication evidence in the abstract. The discovery is a bounded materials result, not a claim that every phase in the full ternary diagram has been exhaustively mapped.

The newly identified molecule 5-(aminomethyl)nicotinonitrile hydroiodide (5ANI) yielded 0.05 cm² devices at 27.22% power-conversion efficiency (27.18% certified) and 21.4 cm² mini-modules at 23.49%. Under the reported ISOS-L-1I operating test, 5ANI devices retained 98.7% of initial efficiency after 1,200 hours.

Technology: SISSO interpretable symbolic regression and NGBoost active-learning models, coupled to DFT calculations and a Bayesian-optimization/symbolic-regression automated fabrication platform

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The team used DFT descriptors and SISSO regression trained on measurements from 20 known passivator/device sets to learn structure–performance relationships. NGBoost active learning reduced the computational cost of estimating interfacial properties across an 18,264-molecule virtual library; model-guided screening selected four candidates for synthesis and experimental validation. 5ANI emerged as a passivator for which the automated device-fabrication loop optimized deposition and processing settings. The ML models guided material choice, while the closed-loop platform refined device fabrication and generated measured feedback.
Test and result
An interpretable machine-learning and active-learning workflow screened a virtual library of 18,264 candidate passivation molecules and guided synthesis/testing of selected candidates for perovskite solar cells.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a result for a specific perovskite composition, cell architecture and passivation/fabrication protocol. The ML regression was trained on only 20 initial known passivator/device datasets; four selected candidates were experimentally synthesized/validated. The reported champion efficiency is a small-area cell result; the mini-module efficiency is lower (23.49%) and laboratory-scale. The 1,200-hour stability result follows the stated ISOS-L-1I protocol and does not establish commercial lifetime. The paper reports high reproducibility from its automated setup, not factory-scale manufacturing. This is a different study and molecule from the 2024 Bayesian-optimized hole-transport materials record (Science DOI 10.1126/science.ads0901): here AI identifies an interfacial passivator 5ANI.

AI contribution
The model used uncertainty-aware exploration and exploitation to select the next formulations for synthesis from a 16,206-composition design space. Experimental feedback from 80 samples across six active-learning iterations updated the Gaussian-process surrogate; model-guided selection yielded three compositions with measured zT above 2. A Gaussian-process model and Bayesian active-learning loop used an average thermoelectric quality factor as a physics-informed descriptor to search a nine-element chalcogenide composition space of 16,206 candidates.

Proposed high-entropy segmented-element efficiencies assume idealized interfaces. The Cu interstitial-cluster mechanism is supported by microscopy/spectroscopy for the characterized sample but is the authors’ interpretation of why performance improves.

7 Jul 2025RMIT University; University of Illinois Chicago; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; Shahid Beheshti University; Monash University; Pakistan Institute of Engineering and Applied Sciences; Concordia University; University of Shanghai for Science and Technology; Australian Synchrotron

Machine-learning-selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 deliver high measured responsivity in extreme-ultraviolet detectors

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A cross-spectral machine-learning model trained on 1,927 visible/UV photodetector records screened materials for extreme-ultraviolet response and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for device validation. At the Australian Synchrotron, the α-MoO3 detector showed measured responsivity of about 50–160 A/W depending on photon energy and bias (about 60–70 A/W near 13.5 nm); ReS2 reached about 20 A/W at 91.8 eV and 1 mV, close to the model estimate. The α-MoO3 device retained repeatable current response through 100 bias cycles under high-flux exposure.

Technology: Extremely Randomized Trees cross-spectral response prediction model

Editorial relevance 60 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model learned relations between material/device descriptors and detector response across wavelength ranges from a 1,927-record dataset of visible and ultraviolet photoresponse measurements. It screened candidate materials for EUV responsivity and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for fabrication and synchrotron testing. The AI contribution was transferring response patterns across spectral domains to prioritize materials; experiments then measured the EUV detector performance.
Test and result
A cross-spectral machine-learning model trained on 1,927 visible/UV photodetector records screened materials for extreme-ultraviolet response and selected α-MoO3 and ReS2 for device validation.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported measurements are for the fabricated devices and stated synchrotron energies, biases and exposure conditions; they do not establish equivalent responsivity across all EUV wavelengths or device architectures. The paper reports α-MoO3 responsivity ranging about 50–160 A/W across test conditions, while near 13.5 nm it reports about 60–70 A/W; ReS2 was tested at a specified energy/bias. The authors' silicon comparison varies with the comparison conditions and metric (the abstract gives about 225-fold, while the device discussion reports up to about 800-fold); this record therefore states the direct responsivity measurements without treating either ratio as universal. The material screening result is a small experimental validation set, not an exhaustive search.

Active learning identifies 28 new DFT-validated pressure-induced phase transitions

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. DFT confirmed 28 previously unreported transformations; 14 high-pressure phases were dynamically stable at transition pressure, including 10 also predicted dynamically stable at zero pressure. The study also identifies a previously unrecorded dynamically stable monoclinic P2₁/c phase of Cr₂O₃.

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

AI contribution
The GNN screened 7,677 phase pairs for consensus transition-pressure predictions. Active learning selected high-confidence pairs for DFT equation-of-state calculations, and the resulting DFT outcomes were added to training data for subsequent cycles. The AI search was the discovery and prioritization mechanism; DFT calculations supplied the physical verification of the transitions.
Test and result
Across 13 active-learning cycles, a graph neural network screened phase pairs for pressure-induced transitions and selected cases for density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations.
Limitation / still unknown
These are computational predictions corroborated by DFT, not experimentally synthesized or observed phases. Of 28 transitions, 14 high-pressure structures were dynamically stable at transition pressure; only 10 were also predicted stable at zero pressure. Two selected phase-pair calculations remained difficult to converge. The paper's discovery count excludes 18 rediscoveries, and individual stability remains subject to DFT approximations.

Generative machine learning guides experimental synthesis of LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga Heusler phases

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

They experimentally synthesized phase-pure LiZn₂Pt and NiPt₂Ga; the measured NiPt₂Ga adopts a tetragonal Heusler structure rather than the model’s cubic proposal, with DFT comparisons supporting its lower energy. This is one paper-level AI-enabled synthesis workflow and three related compounds, not three separate records.

Technology: PGCGM generative Wasserstein GAN for ternary crystal structures; ALIGNN graph neural network for decomposition-enthalpy stability screening

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PGCGM generated candidate crystal structures and ALIGNN screened their predicted stability. Researchers used these model outputs to down-select and choose Heusler-family candidates for synthesis. The authors note that expert judgment remained necessary and that LiZn₂Pt’s composition/structure appeared in the model training databases; NiPt₂Ga’s experimentally realized tetragonal structure was not the exact cubic structure proposed by PGCGM.
Test and result
Researchers combined a generative probabilistic crystal-graph model (PGCGM) with an ALIGNN stability predictor to propose and screen ternary structures, then used the model outputs to guide synthesis.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported synthesis outcome is experimentally characterized in the paper, but the AI was a candidate-generation and stability-screening aid rather than an autonomous discoverer: expert chemistry selected candidates and performed synthesis. LiZn₂Pt’s composition and Fm3̄m structure were already represented in Materials Project/OQMD training data, so its novelty is experimental realization rather than structure invention. The NiPt₂Ga experimental structure is tetragonal P4/mmm, differing from the cubic PGCGM proposal; the paper gives a DFT energy comparison. No superconductivity was observed, and magnetic ordering temperature for NiPt₂Ga was unresolved.

Editorial relevance 47 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Limitation / still unknown
This is a computational materials-property result, not experimental synthesis or electrochemical validation. The oxide structures were drawn from a known candidate space; the authors explicitly define “discovery” here as evaluating a previously unevaluated property, not discovering entirely new compounds. Acid stability is labeled at ΔG_Pourbaix^OER ≤ 0.10 eV/atom, a threshold that allows small positive values on the basis of potential self-passivation. The result depends on HSE06 DFT and the selected Pourbaix phases/conditions; practical catalytic stability must be tested experimentally.

4 Nov 2022Oak Ridge National Laboratory; Argonne National Laboratory; Instituto de Física de Líquidos y Sistemas Biológicos, UNLP-CONICET

Machine-learning-assisted neutron scattering shows hydrostatic pressure tunes interactions in spin ice

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Machine-learning-assisted analysis of diffuse neutron scattering from Dy₂Ti₂O₇ at ambient pressure and about 1.3 GPa extracted pressure-dependent Hamiltonian parameters and found that hydrostatic pressure modifies further-neighbor magnetic interactions and the material’s nanoscale magnetic-glass ordering. The analysis supports using pressure to tune the spin-ice glass state. A transition at substantially higher pressure is a model-based prediction, not an observed transition in this experiment.

Technology: Nonlinear autoencoder, radial-basis generative surrogate and hierarchical clustering for neutron-scattering analysis

Editorial relevance 53 materials Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The nonlinear autoencoder compressed measured and simulated diffuse neutron-scattering volumes; a trained generative surrogate enabled fast forward prediction of scattering from spin-Hamiltonian parameters, while clustering and inverse mapping constrained parameters against the experiment. Those ML components made it practical to analyze pressure-dependent measurements and infer the change in further-neighbor couplings during the neutron experiment workflow.
Test and result
Machine-learning-assisted analysis of diffuse neutron scattering from Dy₂Ti₂O₇ at ambient pressure and about 1.3 GPa extracted pressure-dependent Hamiltonian parameters and found that hydrostatic pressure modifies further-neighbor magnetic interactions and the material’s nanoscale magnetic-glass ordering.
Limitation / still unknown
The reported pressure comparison is between ambient pressure and an estimated hydrostatic pressure of about 1.3 GPa, using separate measurement setups. The change in magnetic couplings and glass morphology is inferred by fitting a spin model to scattering with ML-assisted analysis, not measured as a direct microscopic coupling. The authors predict that substantially higher pressure may induce a phase transition; no such transition was observed here. Some analysis and experimental steering remained manual.

AI contribution
An early-prediction model estimated final cycle life from the first cycles, and Bayesian optimization chose which protocols to test next.
Test and result
224 fast-charging protocols tested experimentally by measuring battery cycle life; high-cycle-life protocols identified in 16 days, versus an estimated 500+ days for exhaustive search without early prediction.

The abstract lists no explicit limitations; generalization to other problems is suggested but not discussed; only the abstract was read.

4 Feb 2020Toyota Central R&D Labs, Inc.

Materials informatics and high-throughput synthesis identify durable oxide-ion conductors

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A machine-learning model trained on literature conductivity data screened inorganic crystal structures and narrowed the chemical space explored by high-throughput synthesis. The study reports high conductivity and thermal durability in selected Ca-(Nb,Ta)-Bi-O compositions; oxygen concentration-cell measurements gave oxide-ion transport numbers around 70–80% at 973 K. The result came from the combined informatics and experimental workflow. It does not establish a pure ionic conductor or room-temperature electrolyte.
